atomicity.reason: One obligation: periodic publication at 100 ms with a 10 ms tolerance while awake; the violation sentence only states the failure criterion of that same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: period, tolerance, scope (vehicle interface, while awake) and the violation criterion are all in the body.

feasibility.reason: A 100 ms frame with a 10 ms tolerance on a vehicle interface is routine and consistent with the linked 100 ms publisher cycle.

parent_fit.reason: Engages the parent's reporting obligation by fixing how often the charge level reaches the vehicle, the timeliness part of 'report how much charge it has left'.

unambiguity.reason: The title demands an 'updated' value every 100 ms, the body only a publication every 100 ms (the linked publisher resends the held value), so it is open whether a repeated stale value counts; and the violation sentence names only late publications while the 10 ms tolerance implies a 90 ms lower bound.
unambiguity.suggestion: Drop 'updated' from the title or say whether a repeated previous value satisfies the requirement, and state whether an early publication (below 90 ms) is a violation.

verifiability.reason: Concrete bus test: record the publication timestamps while awake and require each interval to lie within 100 ms plus or minus 10 ms; a gap beyond 110 ms is an explicit violation.

summary: Crisp, measurable timing requirement; unambiguity reduced by the 'updated' wording and a violation criterion that covers only late publications.
